A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same five-agent coaching study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original results from 31 participants and 155 conversations, including user rankings, questionnaire responses, regression analyses, and expert/LM evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports expert rankings of intended agent behaviors and qualitative findings from formative conversation reviews.

M1.justification: The five Gemini 1.5 Pro agents retain the same coaching and conversation-flow modules. Appendix A.4 prompt templates are unchanged. Revised mappings to expert insights and explanations of module priority do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The participant population, coaching domains, scenario list and selection counts in Table 6 remain unchanged. The added expert-ranking analysis uses the existing 155 transcripts. Education, medicine, and therapy are discussed as possible applications, without new evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparisons retain the same five coaching agents. Figure 2 renames Vanilla to Directive without changing its results. The newly described single-prompt formative example is not an additional comparator evaluated against the proposed agents.

E3.justification: Section 7.6 adds a distinct expert-ranking protocol for six behavioral insights, reporting three experts and 930 annotations over 155 transcripts. Section 6.1 also changes the reported presentation order from randomized order to a balanced Latin square; this does not establish that the user study was rerun.

E4.justification: New Sections 5.1 and 7.6 introduce and evaluate H1-H3, checking whether agents express their intended behaviors. Section 2.2 and Appendix A.1 additionally report formative case-study evidence of premature recommendations and fixated questioning. These add substantial behavioral validation beyond the retained analyses.

E5.justification: The existing regression standard errors, confidence intervals, p-values, and conversation variability summaries are retained. The added expert-ranking results introduce no new uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports expert-ranked outcomes for six insights across all five agents; for example, I1 values are 39.3% for Expert-Facilitative and 21.3% for Base-Facilitative. Formative qualitative findings are also added. Original numerical results in Tables 1-3 and 5-7 and the retained plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the existing statistical analyses remain unchanged. The added H1-H3 predictions and intended/expressed/perceived distinctions are empirical and conceptual rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims about five coaching agents, substance versus style, excessive questioning, and disagreement between evaluation perspectives. The added analyses support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Sections 4 and 7.6 distinguish intended, expressed, and perceived behavior, explaining how adherence to expert insights can coexist with lower user preference. The limitations discussion adds possible applicability beyond health coaching, while retaining the sample-size and model-family limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 identifies the Base prompt used in the formative conversation review, and Section 4.2 clarifies module-priority behavior. v2 also supplies the IRB protocol identifier. Existing agent and auto-evaluation prompts, model identities, and questionnaire details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sharma et al. (2020, 2022) to support distinctions between intended, expressed, and perceived conversational qualities. The main related-work discussion and other cited works are retained; most bibliography differences are formatting changes.

P1.justification: Localized restructuring reorders the six expert insights, replaces the separate C1-C4 exposition with insight-based explanations, and adds interview, hypothesis, and validation subsections. Most existing introduction, results discussion, conclusion, and appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with avatars and moved to the first page, and tables and figures are rearranged. The appendix's qualitative agent-attribute matrix is removed, while a new expert-results Table 4 is added.

improvement.justification: The added expert validation and formative failure examples strengthen the connection between agent design and observed behavior, while the intended/expressed/perceived distinction improves interpretation. The gain is limited by a reporting ambiguity: new Table 4 rows total approximately 100%, although its combined top-two ranking definition would imply 200% across five agents. Its normalization needs clarification, but the added behavioral evidence still provides a modest overall improvement.
